name: DaVinci Fusion Spline Zoom Animation
use_when: A Resolve short needs crisp B-roll zooms, punch-ins, punch-outs, or adjustment-clip motion.
A simple Dynamic Zoom is not enough control.
The agent needs a reusable Fusion motion preset.
A Resolve short uses Dynamic Zoom for a simple first-seconds hook or long emotional passage where manual Fusion control is unnecessary.
avoid_when: The simple cut is not yet working.
The motion would crop faces, captions, proof, or important action.
The clip is too short for the viewer to read the subject after the move.

timeline_pattern.pattern: adjustment_clip_or_clip -> Fusion -> Transform_node -> size_position_keyframes -> Spline -> out_cubic -> adjust_curve -> review_vertical_crop
timeline_pattern.node_rule: Use Transform nodes for size, x/y position, and angle control.
timeline_pattern.spline_rule: Use Spline easing to make the move fast at the start and smooth into the hold.
timeline_pattern.dynamic_zoom_rule: Use Dynamic Zoom for quick automatic in/out moves when manual Fusion control is unnecessary.
timeline_pattern.slow_section_rule: A simple Dynamic Zoom can be enough across a slower emotional section when the subject remains readable.

motion.rule: Animate size and position together, then refine the curve in Spline.

keyframe_values.example_zoom_out: Start Size around 1.95 and animate back to 1.0 for a strong B-roll zoom-out when crop remains safe.
keyframe_values.text_or_graphic_start_size: Start around 0.3-0.5 depending on the text stack and final placement.
keyframe_values.easing: Use Out Cubic as a starting curve for crisp short-form motion.
keyframe_values.flash_transition_peak: For manual flashes, peak opacity at the cut and fade down within a few frames.
keyframe_values.dynamic_hook_window: If Dynamic Zoom is the hook, it should clarify the first 3-5 seconds rather than drift without a focus target.

sound.rule: Pair major zooms or flashes with subtle whooshes or hits only when the motion needs to be felt.

captions.rule: Check caption safe areas after every Fusion scale or position move.

color.rule: No direct color rule; preserve crop readability before adding looks or overlays.

implementation.ffmpeg: Approximate with zoompan/crop/scale expressions and easing curves stored as reusable filter templates.
implementation.remotion: Store Fusion-like presets as transform objects with startScale, endScale, translate, easing, startFrame, endFrame, and holdFrame.
implementation.blender: Use camera or plane transform keyframes with Bezier/eased curves for equivalent zoom moves.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use keyframes or saved animations for zoom-in/zoom-out and manually adjust easing if available.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use adjustment layers or clip Motion keyframes with Ease Out/Ease In and save as presets.

common_mistakes: Leaving the default linear animation because the Spline curve was not adjusted.
Animating only size while the focal point drifts out of frame.
Using a 1.95-style zoom on footage that cannot survive the crop.
Adding Fusion animation before the B-roll placement is motivated.
Opening Fusion for a simple social zoom that Resolve Dynamic Zoom can handle cleanly.
qc: Does the animation ease cleanly instead of feeling linear and slow?
Does the crop preserve face, hands, captions, proof, and action?
Does the move land within 2 frames of the intended beat or spoken reference?
Is the effect reusable without hidden timeline-specific assumptions?
Does the vertical preview stay readable through the whole move?
If Dynamic Zoom is used instead of Fusion, does it still land on a clear story or focus beat?
